# Config-driven status mapping (map-or-drift, collapse round-trip via rebar-status labels)

## Context / Problem

Status mapping is hardcoded in two parity-kept copies —
`value_maps.py` (`LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA`) and `config.py`
(`local_to_jira_status`/`jira_to_local_status`) — with inbound translation in
`inbound_fields.py` (`_JIRA_TO_LOCAL_STATUS`, `_REBAR_STATUS_LABEL_TO_LOCAL`). A Jira
project whose workflow lacks a rebar status (e.g. no `Blocked`) currently has no
echo-safe way to remap it. Status must become config-driven on the S1 core: always
map-or-drift (never skip a whole ticket on status), and a non-injective collapse (two
rebar statuses → one Jira status) must round-trip via the existing `rebar-status:`
annotation label so inbound translation recovers the original rebar status.

## Approach

Wire the S1 `status_map` axis to the outbound and inbound status paths. Outbound: resolve
the effective per-project status map (S1 `resolve_for_project`) over the built-in default
(`LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA`); an unmapped status **drifts** (rebar keeps its status; Jira is
left as-is) with a recorded warning — status never skips a ticket. When a collapse maps
distinct rebar statuses to one Jira status, stamp the existing `rebar-status:<local>`
label (same mechanism `_REBAR_STATUS_LABEL_TO_LOCAL` already consumes) so the round trip
is lossless. Inbound: prefer the `rebar-status:` label, else invert the effective map.
Keep the `value_maps`/`config` parity test green by sourcing both from the resolved map.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/config.py` — route status resolution through S1.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_family/value_maps.py` — built-in
  default becomes the injected fallback.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_fields.py` — label-first inbound recovery.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_status_mapping.py` (new).

## Testing

- **Config-effect contrast (unit, real path):** with a `default.status_map` remapping
  `blocked→"To Do"`, assert an outbound blocked ticket targets `To Do`; with no override,
  assert it targets the built-in default — same read path, different config.
- **Drift (failure path):** an unmapped status leaves Jira unchanged and records the
  drift warning; asserted on the recorded alert, not a crash.
- **Round-trip (collapse):** two rebar statuses collapsed to one Jira status each stamp
  their `rebar-status:` label; inbound recovers each distinct rebar status via
  `_REBAR_STATUS_LABEL_TO_LOCAL` — asserted both directions.
- **Parity:** the existing `value_maps`↔`config` parity test stays green.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Effective status map = built-in ← `default` ← `projects.<KEY>`; a non-default
  overlay changes the outbound target through the real path — verified by
  `test_status_mapping.py::test_status_config_effect`.
- [ ] An unmapped status drifts with a recorded warning and never skips the ticket —
  verified by `test_status_mapping.py::test_unmapped_status_drifts`.
- [ ] A collapsed status round-trips losslessly via `rebar-status:` labels — verified by
  `test_status_mapping.py::test_status_collapse_roundtrip`.
- [ ] The `value_maps`↔`config` parity test remains green.

Test tier: **in-process unit** — outbound/inbound translation are pure functions over the
resolved map; the oracle is the produced target field / recorded alert / recovered status.
